Hi Marissa,

Thanks for a productive call earlier — good to meet you and the team. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can align engineering for a POC: 

- Goal: Evaluate Redwood for search + assistant across our internal docs. Key needs are embeddings + reranker, structured tool-calling for internal ticket lookups, and strong prompt governance (versioning + injection mitigations).
- Technical asks: sample SDK integration for our node/python services; recommended auth (service account vs API key), options for private VPC deployment, routing policies if we want a low-cost fallback model, and examples of structured output / tool-calling schemas.

Samir —

Great to meet you too. Appreciate the clear recap. I attached a short integration guide and our first-pass prompt templates doc to kick off. High-level answers below and a proposed next step schedule: 

1) SDK & auth
- We have production SDKs for Node and Python with examples for streaming/chat + embeddings. See attached redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf.
- Auth options: API keys for hosted (quick start), service accounts + JWTs for Dedicated/Private, and mTLS for on-prem. For secrets, integrate with your KMS; we support customer-managed KMS for Private.

2) Routing & fallbacks
- You can configure routing policies by latency, cost tier, or region. Common pattern: primary model for quality + a quantized fallback for burst/budget-sensitive requests. We can demo automatic fallback rules in the console.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- Templates for tool calling and schema validation are included in prompt-templates-v1.md. We support a JSON-schema-backed structured output layer and first-class tool-calling primitives in the SDK.

4) Embeddings & reranking
- We expose embeddings endpoints and a reranker primitive that scores candidate documents. For POC, we recommend small-batch embeddings + an in-memory ANN (we have an example using FAISS) and a two-stage reranker to cut down latency and cost.

5) Prompt governance & red-teaming
- Version prompts in Git with a manifest file (we included a checklist). Start with immutable production prompt version tags and a shadow/tagged rollout for canarying. For injection mitigations, we recommend: strict schema validation for tool calls, input sanitization layers, output constraints (max tokens/format validators), and adversarial tests as part of CI.

Next steps / proposed schedule:
- Technical deep-dive (90 min): Mon 2026-11-29 10am PT / alternate Tue 11/30 9am PT
- Engineering checklist + pre-reqs: provide a sandbox account, sample dataset links, and a list of third-party tools you want to call.

CC'ing Dylan to add a couple technical notes and to bring security artifacts. I'll send calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Samir — quick technical notes from our infra side: 

- SDK setup: The Node SDK example in the guide shows both API key and service-account flows. For gRPC streaming, we recommend increasing the connection window and enabling automatic reconnects in unstable networks.

- Auth: For production PII workloads we suggest Dedicated or Private with service accounts + short-lived JWTs minted by your identity provider. If you use our hosted API temporarily, rotate API keys frequently and scope them per-project.

- Routing: If you want deterministic low-latency, pin critical routes to a dedicated pool. For cost-flex, create a policy: primary model -> reranker -> budget fallback. We also support per-route caching (prefix caching) which helps with chat-like repeated prompts.

- Structured tool-calling: Enforce an output schema on the model side (SDK includes a validator helper) and implement a strict runner for any tool invocation — only allow pre-registered tool IDs and validate arguments server-side.

- Embeddings/reranker: Use float16 quantized embeddings for storage, but keep scoring on fp32 for rerank step if latency allows. We can share a sample notebook that wires Redwood embeddings -> FAISS -> reranker.

- Prompt governance/versioning: Store prompt templates in a Git repo with a manifest (version, owner, tests). CI should run a red-team suite (adversarial prompts) and a suite of golden-path evals. For rollback, we tag the last-known-good prompt and have a simple toggle in the runtime to pin to a version.

I'll prepare the notebook and a short playbook for red-teaming scenarios (injection, hallucination triggers, tool-call escalation).

— Dylan (Infra Engineering)
